info.syllabusName: Introduction to Linguistics - Dẫn luận ngôn ngữ
info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
info.description:
The Study of Language offers:
- a fundamental introduction to language study
- a vocabulary for talking about language and a solid knowledge of how English works.
- major concepts in language study through all the key elements of language are presented
info.studentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments, and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptops in class only for learning purposes
info.tools:
Course book
Tech Tools:
- ChatGPT: Summarize and ask questions; generate timelines and explanations of language evolution, generate examples of compounding, blending, borrowing, etc
- Google AI Phonetic Transcriber (toPhonetics Converter): Convert speech to IPA for phonetic analysis
- Grammarly: Check usage in context and suggest alternatives.
- Linguakit/Syntactic analyzer : Analyze sentence structure and semantic roles; Semantic role labeling and contextual analysis.
- DeepL Translator: Compare semantic shifts between Vietnamese and English; Analyze meaning shifts in translation
- Discourse Analyzer AI Toolkit: Analyse texts in discourses, pragmatics and implicature
- Duolingo: Track progress in English learning.
- Coursera: Take online courses in linguistics and language learning.
info.note:
On-going marks:
- 02 assignments: 40%
- 2 Quizzes: 10%
01 Final project: 50%

Conditions to pass:
Each on-going mark: > 0
Grade Average >= 5/10

clos.loDetails: Distinguish the sounds and the sound patterns of laguage
Report the importance of word formation and describe processes involved in word formation.
Identify referential meaning and relationships between words; examine the importance of context that contributes to meaning
Demonstrate neurolinguistics and the process of first and second language asquisition
Have a spirit of self-study, lifelong learning
Have a professional working attitude, and have ability to work in a team

assessments.knowledgeSkill: The project will assess the knowledge and application of course learning outcomes from the delivered chapters. Questions will be based on the key topics covered in each chapter.
assessments.gradingGuide:
*by exam board, using computer.
* Written Deliverables: Students must submit all written components of the project to the Examination Office by the end of Week 10. The Examination Office will then forward the submissions to the teacher responsible for marking the presentation;
*Presentation: Students will present their project findings in a 20 -minute presentation and 5-minute Q&A during the final examination period.
*Students will work in groups of 4 members. In cases where the total number of students does not allow for equal grouping, teams of three or five members may be formed to accommodate the class size.
assessments.note:
If a student's project does not meet the required standards, the teacher should provide constructive feedback to guide improvement. This will enable the student to revise both the written component and the presentation, and resubmit their work prior to delivering the updated presentation during the resit examination period.
- Components:
1. Written components: 50%
2. Presentation: 50%
